# Runic Classes

The class lore exactly as it ships in the class selection screen. Each class names its craft, its two Aptitudes (primary first), what its Runic Mark, Seal and Crown feel like, and its place in a company. Numbers live in the Perk and Power tooltips, not here.

## Barbarian

A **Barbarian** fights from the gut. Their craft is **Fury**: the heat that rises as the wounds pile up, turning every hit they take into a reason to hit back harder. Barbarians run on **Strength** first and **Constitution** second; their Runic Mark answers a bloodied blow with a heavier one, their Seal turns a kill into a roar that clears the ground around them, and their Crown is the moment a crushing hit makes them harder to stop rather than easier. In a company they stand where the fighting is thickest and draw it toward themselves. Some found the Fury in hard country, some in the fighting pits, and some simply found it waiting when nothing else was left.

## Fighter

A **Fighter** is the soldier the rest of the company stands behind. Their craft is **Drill**: the thousand repetitions that turn a sword, an axe or a spear into an extension of the arm, and a shield into a wall that answers back. Fighters run on **Strength** first and **Endurance** second; their Runic Mark rewards the patient first cut, their Seal turns a raised shield into cover for everyone beside them, and their Crown is the last stand that refuses to end a fight on anyone's terms but theirs. Knights, caravan guards and sellswords all drill the same forms. What they do with the forms is their own business.

## Monk

A **Monk** carries nothing they cannot carry inside themselves. Their craft is **Breath**: the steady rhythm that keeps the body light, the hands quick and the mind still, so that an open palm lands like a blade. Monks run on **Dexterity** first and **Endurance** second; their Runic Mark opens a guard with a single precise strike, their Seal gathers a flurry of blows into one shuddering impact, and their Crown lets a perfectly centred body slip a blow that should have broken it. In a company they move where others cannot, unburdened and unhurried. Some learned the Breath in quiet halls, some on the road, and some taught themselves.

## Rogue

A **Rogue** wins before the other side knows a fight has started. Their craft is **Edgework**: the precise placement of one blade, one lockpick, one quiet step. Rogues run on **Dexterity** first and **Fortune** second; their Runic Mark opens a fight with a cut that marks the target, their Seal lets a kill fold them back into the dark, and their Crown collects on every wound they have opened at once. Some work the alleys of a city, some the halls beneath a ruin. All of them prefer one perfect strike to a hundred honest ones.

## Ranger

A **Ranger** keeps **The Long Watch** over the places between settlements: the forest edges, the high passes and the long roads where help is days away. Their craft is patience at a distance, reading a trail, a wind and a bowstring together until the shot is already decided. Rangers run on **Dexterity** first and **Wisdom** second; their Runic Mark sends a second arrow after a long first one, their Seal pins a quarry where it stands, and their Crown answers a run of clean hits with a volley that fills the sky. In a company they see the danger first and settle it before it closes. The animals that walk beside them fight a little harder for it.

## Bard

A **Bard** turns a fight into a performance and a company into a chorus. Their craft is **Cadence**: the rhythm of verse, drum and voice that steadies an ally's hands and sours an enemy's footing. Bards run on **Intelligence** first and **Fortune** second; their Runic Mark opens an encounter with a verse that quickens everyone near, their Seal answers a strike with a discord that weakens every foe around it, and their Crown is the anthem that catches a falling friend. Bards learn quickly, bargain well and travel light. Wherever a company gathers, the Bard is the reason it holds together a little longer than anyone expected.

## Cleric

A **Cleric** carries the **Rites**: the spoken forms through which a chosen power reaches into the world to mend, to ward and to break what should not walk. Clerics run on **Wisdom** first and **Magic** second; their Runic Mark turns a fallen undead into light for their companions, their Seal shields an ally the moment a blow lands too hard, and their Crown makes every healing a rallying call. Temples train them, but the Rites answer anyone who keeps them faithfully, altar or no altar.

## Druid

A **Druid** keeps **The Green Covenant**: a promise between the one who tends the wild and the wild that tends them back. Bark hardens under their feet, rain mends them and crops grow faster in their company. Druids run on **Magic** first and **Endurance** second; their Runic Mark lets a vine catch whatever they strike, their Seal wraps them in thorns that answer a heavy blow, and their Crown calls the whole grove to their side when they falter. In a company they are the one who keeps everyone fed and on their feet. Some keep the Covenant in deep forest, some at the edge of a single field.

## Sorcerer

A **Sorcerer** was born with magic already running through them. Their craft is the **Wild Vein**: a current of power they never studied for, only learned to ride, and that answers best when it is pushed. Sorcerers run on **Magic** first and **Constitution** second, because a body that carries the Vein grows strong enough to bear it; their Runic Mark sharpens a first strike against an untouched foe, their Seal returns what a killing spell spent, and their Crown lets the Vein surge outward in a burst no one, not even the Sorcerer, can quite predict. In a company they are the spark that turns a stand-off into a rout.

## Warlock

A **Warlock** struck a deal and keeps collecting on it. Their craft is **The Bargain**: power taken on terms and repaid in the lives of their enemies and the luck of the draw. Warlocks run on **Magic** first and **Fortune** second; their Runic Mark drinks a little life from any weakened foe, their Seal spreads the shadow of a kill across everything nearby, and their Crown is the moment the debt comes due and every enemy in reach pays it at once. Who sits across the table from a Warlock is their own affair, and most prefer it that way. In a company they are the one the enemy least wants to get close to.

## Wizard

A **Wizard** treats magic as a discipline to be mastered. Their craft is **The Study**: notes, diagrams and patient repetition until a working is understood rather than merely cast. Wizards run on **Intelligence** first and **Magic** second; their Runic Mark strikes harder against any creature they have studied before, their Seal reclaims the effort a successful spell spent, and their Crown is a grand working built from a run of lesser ones. Wizards enchant with a keen eye and learn faster than anyone. In a company they are the reference everyone checks before trying something dangerous, and the reason the dangerous thing works.

## Artificer

An **Artificer** blends rune-lore with mechanical engineering to make better gear. Rather than waving a wand, an Artificer works magic through artisans' tools, laying it into an item as clockwork, as a mixture or as a rune cut into steel. Their defining craft is **Infusions**: refinements that make the tools and weapons they build tougher, sharper and luckier than the recipe promises. Artificers run on **Intelligence** first and **Tinkering** second; their Runic Mark turns any working tool into a weapon, their Seal mends a failing tool at the last moment, and their Crown stores every hit in a capacitor until it arcs outward. In a company they are the problem-solver who keeps everyone's gear in fighting shape.

## Paladin

A **Paladin** is bound by **The Oath**: a promise to stand between harm and the people who cannot stand against it. The Oath hardens them and everyone close to them, and it does not let a companion fall while the Paladin still stands. Paladins run on **Constitution** first and **Wisdom** second; their Runic Mark answers anyone who wounds a friend, their Seal turns a held shield into protection for the whole line, and their Crown is the avatar the Oath makes of them when the fight turns desperate. Some swear the Oath at an altar, some in a storm, some over a grave. Every one of them keeps it.

## Classless

To be **Classless** is to walk your own road. A Classless adventurer takes no class Perks, no class Powers and no head start in any Aptitude, and answers to no discipline: every level they earn goes wherever they choose. Many begin this way and take up a class later with a Class Orb. Some never do, and are proud of it.
